newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Dresdner 1996 profit up over 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dresdner 1996 profit up over 40 pct.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG on Thursday reported a stronger-than-expected rise of more than 40 percent in operating profit last year, outperforming its top domestic rivals in part due to proceeds from dissolving hidden reserves.
Dresdner, Germany's second-largest bank, said group operating profit after risk provisions rose to more than 2.8 billion marks from 1.99 billion, according to preliminary data.
It also planned to raise its dividend for 1996 to 1.45 marks from 1.35 marks and pay an additional 10 pfennig per share bonus to commemorate the bank's 125th anniversary.
Analysts had expected a smaller rise in operating profit, by 30 percent to about 2.6 billion.

Dresdner said almost half the increase in profit stemmed from earnings on its liquidity portfolio amid gains from the sale of bond holdings in early 1996 as well as proceeds from the sale of share stakes of under five percent.
Dresdner also said it was transferring more than 800 million marks to its reserves.
"Commission income developed very favourably, while both net interest income and ... trading income were also clearly above 1995 results," the bank said in a brief statement.
Provisions for loan losses were only slightly higher than the previous year when they totalled a gross 1.075 billion marks.
The bank gave no net profit figure and provided no further details. It will report its full final results in April. Analysts expect its net profit to have risen 30 percent to 1.57 billion marks.

Dresdner's earnings were partly driven by British investment bank unit Kleinwort Benson, included in group accounts for a full 12 months last year compared with just three months in 1995 when it was consolidated in September, analysts said.

Dresdner is also expected to have received a late boost in commission income from the flotation of state telephone monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG in November, for which it was one of the three global coordinators.

Analysts said Dresdner will not be able to repeat its 1996 performance in 1997 since it would no longer benefit from the effect of Kleinwort's inclusion and because it is not expected to realise hidden reserve on the same scale as last year.

"Dresdner's earnings development will be moderate this year," said Andreas Thielen, banking analyst at Enskilda Securities in London. "It had a high earnings contribution from dissolving reserves, that won't be repeated."

But Thielen added that German banking stocks would continue to profit from speculation of mergers in the sector. Dresdner's share price has risen 18.8 percent this year to 53.80 marks at Thursday's bourse close, almost matching a 21 percent jump in the shares of Deutsche Bank AG, Europe's largest bank.

Dresdner's results come just one week after rating agency Moody's Investors Service said it may downgrade Dresdner's top Aaa long-term debt rating because the German banking sector as a whole was coming under pressure from stronger competition, narrower lending yields and flatter loan demand.
The earnings end the preliminary reporting season for Germany's top five banks and show Dresdner outperforming most of its main domestic competitors in terms of earnings growth.
Deutsche this week reported a 37 percent rise in operating profit to 5.8 billion marks but its net profit profit grew just 4.8 percent.

Munich-based Bayerische Vereinsbank AG said its operating profit grew 16 percent last year while Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG said its operating profit fell nine percent amid a sharp rise in risk provisions.
Commerzbank AG, Germany's third-largest bank, last month reported a 22 percent jump in net profit. It has not yet given a figure for operating profit.
